body:
The error is coming from https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/ab4ab090667e96c0e8a2623e33573ae06be14b54/activerecord/lib/active_record/connection_adapters/postgresql/oid/range.rb#L20-L32

The value comes in as `"(,\"2020-08-22 00:00:00\"]"`, then we try to cast it to a range by extracting out `from` as `-Float::INFINITY` and `to` as a `Time`. Unfortunately it is not possible to create a range from `-Float::INFINITY` to a `Time`:

```rb
-Float::INFINITY..Date.tomorrow.to_time
#=> ArgumentError (bad value for range)
```

@composerinteralia @kamipo 

I see different solutions:
1. This can be resolved by a Float monkey-patch (maybe as part of ActiveSupport):
```
class Float
  alias_method :original_compare, :<=>
  def <=>(other)
    if other.is_a? Time
      -(other <=> self)
    else
      original_compare(other)
    end
  end
end
```
But I don't how I feel about that. 

2. Updating Ruby itself to support `-Float::INFINITY..Time.new` (as well as `Time.new..Float::INFINITY`) on the native level. This would not require any changes on the Rails side but it will take some time to release the new Ruby version. ([Rejected by Matz](https://bugs.ruby-lang.org/issues/17169))

3. Use `nil` instead of `Infinity`
Ruby 2.7+ supports both Beginsless and Endless ranges
Ruby 2.6+ supports only Endless ranges
Ruby 2.5 (current ActiveRecord ruby version) can only use `Time.new..Float::INFINITY` due to an ActiveSupports Time monkey-patch
    1. Bump up ruby version from `2.5` to `2.7` and use Beginless/Endless ranges
    2. Make ActiveRecord support both `Infinity` and `nil` approaches when casting ranges based on the current ruby version (So if you use Rails with Ruby 2.7+ you should be able to use these PostgreSQL ranges with rails)

Thoughts?

I ran into this today as well. The solution above that monkey-patches float seems extremely convenient, but I also totally understand the concerns with doing that. (The degree to which ActiveSupport and many Ruby gems monkey-patch built-in stuff really gave me pause when I first picked up both Ruby and Rails.)

I’d be happy with any solution that makes these values accessible, whether it’s 3.ii (3.i seems like imposing an unreasonable upgrade burden on lots of Rails users), a custom range type for this situation (then we could also support ranges that exclude the start value), or even if ActiveRecord just gave me back the Postgres string representation (`'[-infinity,2020-08-22 00:00:00]'`) and also let me set it using the string. (This last one is definitely the worst solution, but it’s still better than not being able to read a value like this at all.)

issue.title: Allow pages to have multiple URLs

repository.name: web-monitoring-db
repository.description: An HTTP API for tracking and annotating changes to a set of web pages.

issue.body:
**This is an idea/open question that I’d like to resolve relatively quickly.**

We’ve avoided figuring out how to best model pages that move or have multiple locations over time (and probably at the same time, too). While doing some routine updates today, I discovered that the domain http://www.cpc.noaa.gov/ was just shut down earlier this month. It looks like all those pages have been redirecting to identical paths at https://www.cpc.ncep.noaa.gov/ for quite a while (months, maybe longer?) and they’ve finally stopped responding to the older domain.

In the long term, we need to actually model this correctly. In the short term, we need to keep monitoring these pages, so my quick-and-dirty suggestion is to add a `notes` text field to the Page record in DB, update the `url` field for those pages, and add some human-readable text to the `notes` field describing the situation for for those pages.

Thoughts?

/cc @jsnshrmn @danielballan @gretchengehrke

body: Given the rejection of option 2, I think 3.ii is the most reasonable option.

issue.title: Fix deserializing infinite ranges from time-based range columns in PostgreSQL
issue.body:
Fixes #39833. See its description for context.

Ruby does not support `Time.now..Float::INFINITY`-like ranges, and since the minimum required ruby version is 2.7, we can use beginless/endless ranges. So this PR implements the use of beginless/endless ranges for all PostgreSQL `range` type columns.

Before: `thing.numeric_range # => 1..Float::INFINITY`
After: `thing.numeric_range # => 1..`

This is potentially a breaking change, since while functionally equivalent, but `1..Float::INFINITY != 1..`.

issue.title: Support unbounded time ranges for PostgreSQL
issue.body:
Ruby raises an `ArgumentError` when mixing `Time` and `Float` values in a `Range`, such as `Time.now..Float::INFINITY`.  Therefore, when deserializing time ranges, we must use a beginless range to represent a range with no lower bound, or an endless range to represent a range with no upper bound.

Fixes #39833.
Closes #45082.

---

This is an alternative to #45082 that should not break existing code.  @fatkodima, I've added you as a co-author.
